recipes.name: Savoiardi (Ladyfingers)
recipes.flavorProfile: Light, dry and crisp, with a sugary crust and an eggy sweetness.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light biscuit made mostly of egg, sugar and flour, with no butter.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

ingredients.prepNote: in place of a sachet of vanillin

instructions: Whisk the yolks with half the sugar, the lemon zest and the vanilla until pale and thick. Whip the whites to soft peaks, then add the rest of the sugar and whip to firm peaks.
Fold the whites into the yolks, then fold in the flour and starch in two parts.
Pipe 10 cm fingers onto lined trays, dust with icing sugar, wait 5 minutes and dust again, then bake at 190 °C (375 °F) for about 10 minutes, until lightly golden.
Cool and keep in a tin. Dry ones soak up coffee best.

nutritionHighlights.note: About 1.5 g per biscuit, from the eggs.

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore, Savoiardi for every amount and step; 4 eggs, 100 g sugar, 50 g 00 flour, 50 g potato starch, vanillin, grated zest of 1 lemon, icing sugar dusted twice; 190 °C for 10 minutes.

recipes.name: Gelato Fior di Latte
recipes.flavorProfile: Clean, milky and lightly sweet, with no egg or vanilla.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lower in fat than custard ice cream, since it is mostly milk, and it still brings calcium.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Heat the milk, cream and sugar to 85 C (185 F), stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Chill overnight.
Churn in an ice cream maker and serve soft, or freeze briefly. One serving is a 60 g scoop.

citations.source: Ricette che passione (GialloZafferano blog), Gelato fior di latte

recipes.curationNote: Ricette che passione (GialloZafferano blog), Gelato fior di latte for every amount and step; 400 g milk, 250 g cream, 100 g sugar; Gambero Rosso and other versions run from 500 g milk with 80 g cream to more cream; ours (750 ml milk, 250 ml cream, 170 g sugar) sits inside that range.

recipes.name: Pangrattato (Dry Breadcrumbs)
recipes.flavorProfile: Plain and toasty, from unsalted country bread.
recipes.healthBenefit: Made from bread with no salt, so it adds no sodium.
instructions: Cut the stale loaf in slices and dry them in a 120 C (250 F) oven for about 1 hour, until crisp right through.
Cool and grind fine, then sift. Keep in a closed jar for a month.

nutritionHighlights.note: Almost none, since Tuscan bread has no salt.

recipes.name: Pancetta (Cured Pork Belly)
recipes.flavorProfile: Salty, sweet-fatted pork belly with black pepper, fennel seed, nutmeg and garlic.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork belly brings B vitamins and zinc; used a little at a time to season a dish.

ingredients.baseName: Gris sidfläsk bit rå m. svål
ingredients.cutPrep: skin removed, in one flat piece

ingredients.prepNote: all of it taken up by the meat

instructions: Mix the salt, sugar, pepper, nutmeg, fennel seed, thyme and garlic and rub it into every side of the belly.
Seal in a bag and keep in the fridge 7 to 10 days, turning daily, until it is firm all through.

Rinse, pat dry and hang it flat (tesa) in a dark, cool, airy place at about 16 °C (60 °F) and about 60 percent humidity for at least 1 week, until it has lost about a third of its weight. One serving is 50 g.

nutritionHighlights.note: Most of the weight is fat.

recipes.curationNote: Stefan's Gourmet Blog, Homemade pancetta for every amount and step; 1.5 kg belly: 45 g salt, 22.5 g pepper, 22.5 g sugar, 4.5 g nutmeg, 7.5 g fennel seed, 7.5 g dried thyme, 3 garlic cloves, no nitrite; scaled to our 1.85 kg.

recipes.name: Guanciale (Cured Pork Cheek)
recipes.flavorProfile: Rich, sweet pork fat cured with salt, black pepper and garlic.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork fat carries flavour; a little goes into a whole pot of pasta.

ingredients.baseName: Gris sidfläsk bit rå m. svål
ingredients.prepNote: in place of pork cheek (jowl), which the database does not hold; the cut is close in fat and meat
all of it taken up by the meat

instructions: Rub the salt, sugar, pepper and garlic all over the cheek (or belly).
Seal it in a bag and keep it in the fridge for 1 week, turning it every day.
Rinse it, pat it dry and hang it in a cool, airy place at about 16 °C (60 °F) for about 4 weeks, until firm and much lighter. One serving is 50 g.
recipes.curationNote: Stefan's Gourmet Blog, Homemade guanciale for every amount and step; 1.2 kg jowl with 35 g salt, 17.5 g pepper, 17.5 g sugar and 2 garlic cloves; scaled to our 1 kg.

recipes.name: Lardo (Cured Pork Back Fat)
recipes.flavorProfile: Silky white fat cured with rosemary, garlic, black pepper, thyme, star anise and bay.
recipes.healthBenefit: Almost all fat; it is eaten in thin slices or melted into a dish.
instructions: Mix the salt, sugar, rosemary, garlic powder, pepper, thyme, star anise and bay. The recipe allows 5 g smoked salt and 4 g curing salt No. 2 as well, which it uses as a guard against listeria and botulism; neither is counted here.
Weigh the mix, divide it in half and massage one half into each piece of fat. Vacuum seal each piece with its cure.
Set the packs in a container, cover with a plate smaller than the opening and weigh it down. Cure in the fridge 12 days, turning every 3 days.

Rinse well and pat dry. Run a string through one corner, wrap in cheesecloth and then loosely in foil to keep out light, and hang somewhere dark at 45 to 60°F (7 to 16°C) and 65 to 75% humidity for at least 2 weeks, better 4 to 8.
Slice very thin. One serving is 20 g.

nutritionHighlights.note: About 2 g per 20 g, from the cure.

citations.source: Cup of Yum, Lardo (Cured Pork Fatback)

recipes.curationNote: Cup of Yum's home lardo, every amount kept for 1 kg of fat; it makes about 2 lb. The optional smoked salt and curing salt are named in the steps and left out of the count.

recipes.name: Prosciutto Crudo (Dry-Cured Ham)
recipes.flavorProfile: Sweet, delicate and salty, from long air-drying.
recipes.healthBenefit: Ham brings protein, B vitamins and zinc; it is salty, so it goes far in small amounts.

ingredients.prepNote: the part the ham keeps; about 1 kg more is rubbed on and brushed off

instructions: Rub the leg with salt, more on the skin and less on the meat, and keep at 1 to 4 C (34 to 39 F) for a week. Brush off, salt again and leave 2 to 3 weeks more.
Brush off the salt and rest the ham 2 to 3 months in a cold room so the salt spreads through.
Hang in a cool, airy place for at least 12 months, until it has lost about a third of its weight. Slice paper thin. One serving is 50 g.

recipes.name: Speck Alto Adige (Smoked Cured Ham)
recipes.flavorProfile: Smoky, juniper-scented cured ham, firmer and saltier than prosciutto.
recipes.healthBenefit: Ham brings protein, B vitamins and zinc.

ingredients.cutPrep: boned and split into flat pieces

ingredients.prepNote: all of it taken up by the meat

ingredients.name: Cure #2 (curing salt with nitrite and nitrate)
ingredients.prepNote: 2.5 g per kg of meat, weighed exactly

instructions: Rub the salt, Cure #2, pepper, bay, garlic powder, rosemary, nutmeg and juniper into the meat, seal it and keep it in the fridge for 21 days, turning it every day or so.
Dry it for about 15 days at around 20 °C (68 °F), cold smoking it about 4 hours a day over beech and never above 20 °C (68 °F).
Hang it in a cool, airy room at 10 to 15 °C (50 to 59 °F) for 6 to 12 months, until it has lost about a third of its weight. One serving is 50 g.

citations.source: Taste of Artisan, Homemade dry cured speck

recipes.curationNote: Taste of Artisan, Homemade dry cured speck for every amount and step; per 1 kg leg: 29.5 g salt, 2.5 g Cure #2, 0.5 g bay, 0.5 g juniper, 2 g pepper, 2 g garlic powder, 0.5 g nutmeg, 2 g ground rosemary; scaled to our 5 kg.

recipes.name: Salsiccia (Fresh Italian Pork Sausage)
recipes.flavorProfile: Coarse, juicy pork sausage with garlic, black pepper and white wine.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork brings protein, B vitamins and zinc; no fillers.

ingredients.baseName: Gris sidfläsk bit rå m. svål
Pork, offal and by-products, small intestine
ingredients.prepNote: about 2 m for 1 kg of filling

instructions: Mix the ground meat with the salt, pepper, garlic and wine until it just holds together. Keep everything cold.
Stuff into the hog casing and twist into 10 links of about 100 g.
Rest overnight in the fridge. Cook within 3 days or freeze. To use without the skin, slit and peel it off.

citations.source: Stefan's Gourmet Blog, Homemade Italian pork sausage

recipes.curationNote: Stefan's Gourmet Blog, Homemade Italian pork sausage (salsiccia fatta in casa) for every amount and step; 500 g meat (75% shoulder, 25% belly), 1.8% salt, 0.3% pepper, 10% white wine, 1% garlic; scaled to our 1 kg.
